GEOPHYSICS
A New 254 Ma Paleomagnetic Pole of the East European Platform:
The Moscow Syneclise, the Sukhoborka and Sosnovka Sections
A. M. Fetisovaa,b,*, R. V. Veselovskiya,b, and V. K. Golubevc
Presented by Academician L.N. Kogarko January 27, 2023
Received February 10, 2023; revised February 17, 2023; accepted February 21, 2023
Abstract—The results of paleomagnetic and rock magnetic studies of the upper Permian red beds from the
Sukhoborka and Sosnovka sections of the south-eastern of the Moscow syneclise on the right bank of the Vet-
luga River in Nizhny Novgorod Region, Russia, are presented. The arguments in favor of the primary nature
of the characteristic magnetization component are indicated. The first late Permian (254 Ma) paleomagnetic
pole dated precisely for the sedimentary Permian–Triassic complex in the eastern part of the East European
Platform is calculated: 56.731°N, 45.748°E, N = 44, plat = 55.3°, plong = 158.1°, dp/dm = 3.5°/5.1°,
paleolat = 34.6°.
Keywords: paleomagnetism, East European Platform, Russian Plate, Permian, paleomagnetic pole
DOI: 10.1134/S1028334X2360038X

n is the number of single paleomagnetic directions (the number of samples); D and I are declination and inclination, respectively; K is
concentration parameter; α95 is the radius of the 95% confidence circle; slat and slong are the coordinates of sampling site; plat and
plong are the latitude and longitude of the paleomagnetic pole; dp/dm are the semiaxes of the 95% confidence oval; paleolat is the
paleolatitude of the sampling site; AF and TD are the alternating magnetic field and thermal demagnetization, respectively; N and R are
the normal and reversed polarities of the characteristic remanent magnetization (ChRM); f is the inclination shallowing coefficient.

netic demagnetization of the samples: (a, b) thermal demag and (c) alternating field demag. Geographic coordinate system.

ponents of normal (blue), reversed (pink, the empty circle), and normal and reversed (red) polarity with 95% confidence circles.
Filled (empty) circles in the stereograms are the vector projections onto the lower (upper) hemisphere; filled (empty) circles in
the Zijderveld diagrams are the vector projections onto the horizontal (vertical) planes.

cient f = 0.6 and f = 0.9, respectively. The colored squares show the EEP paleomagnetic poles obtained for the objects within the
Russian Plate in [6‒8]; the color corresponds to the pole age. The gray circles are the 95% confidence circles.
